change: Anchor identity gate before descending: the anchor used here resolved about 70 mm from the validated garment centre with only ~0.5 mm of relief, i.e. inboard shoulder/armhole cloth at effectively tabletop height, not the outer-distal gathered sleeve the objective names. Require that the resolved metric position lie in the outer-distal sleeve band consistent with previously grounded sleeve anchors, and that engaged height fall inside measured relief of the chosen structure, before any closure.

Retire the sub-table closing plane as an experimental dimension: this closure was commanded 1.5 mm below the measured table plane and still produced a full-travel empty close with no cloth rising and no visible surface disturbance, so driving the closing plane under a flat seated ply does not create capture.

Retire single-anchor pinching of this sleeve as a contact family: seven closures across featureless interior, outer band, inclined outboard edge-straddle, an off-target torso-side bite, the thickest measured stack on the garment, and now a sub-table plane all produced identical empty jaws, so height, relief magnitude, contact location, and closing-plane depth are all excluded.

Escalate to two-contact opposition, where one contact immobilizes cloth well away from the separation point by weight, pinning, or downward hold so opposition exists before any peel or lift, or target a mechanically verified free fabric boundary with visible interior passage or light between plies on both sides.

Note the gripper telemetry here is flagged simulated and never reports state=grasp, so it cannot serve as that gate on its own and must be paired with a visual hold check.

If no gathered structure actually exists, REPAIR_SLEEVE has no target and the correct next action is the ordered inward fold attempt rather than an eighth repair variant.

That fails the pre-closure consistency gate, so this iteration did not test the sleeve repair hypothesis at all and its null result is evidence about anchor identity and closure geometry only. Acquisition then failed for the seventh consecutive time: the hold-check still shows the shirt flat and fully seated with the gripper unoccluded above it and nothing suspended, all 16 Camera C tiles show a static silhouette, and telemetry reads full jaw travel with no contact. Both structural hypotheses are contradicted rather than unknown, because a separable layer would have tented while far landmarks stayed seated, and a rolled curl would have tightened or extended its footprint; neither appears. The one fresh hypothesis this action did test, a closing plane below the table plane, is falsified, which together with the previously excluded height, relief magnitude, and contact location leaves no untested single-anchor variable. Transport and laydown ran on empty jaws and must not be re-tuned. Because a genuinely different and safely grounded experiment still exists, correcting anchor identity to the outer-distal sleeve band while escalating to two-contact opposition or a mechanically verified free boundary, the change list is non-empty; but if opposition is not expressible with the available primitives, the honest conclusion is an infrastructure limit rather than another variant.

skill_update.name: null-change-missed-grasp-recovery
skill_update.purpose: Recognise a near-null garment action, separate a clean miss from a contact-without-hold on a compressible pile, reject a closure whose resolved anchor or engaged height is inconsistent with the visually chosen structure, and additionally retire driving the closing plane beneath the support surface as a way to capture a flat seated ply.
skill_update.guidance: Keep the existing null-change and contact-without-hold checks, the escalation rule, and the pre-closure consistency gate on resolved anchor identity and engaged height. Add this lesson about closure depth on thin, flat, fully seated cloth. When a chosen reference measures only a fraction of a millimetre above the support surface, the temptation is to reason that no plane above the surface can enclose the ply and therefore to command closure below the surface plane. Treat that as a dead end rather than a remaining degree of freedom: a single ply pressed flat against a hard surface offers no opposition, so jaws arriving at or beneath its top face still sweep across it and meet with nothing between them, and the attempt adds surface-contact risk without adding diagnostic value. Record such an outcome as evidence that closure depth is exhausted as a dimension, not as evidence about the pull direction, pull distance, deposit region, or release, all of which remain untested. More importantly, treat a near-surface measurement at the intended anchor as a signal that the visually chosen raised structure was never actually resolved: re-ground onto a location whose measured relief matches the structure seen in the images, and if no such location exists, question whether the raised structure exists at all before planning another closure. Once closure depth, contact location, relief magnitude, and entry axis have all been varied without any independent cloth rising in a post-close hold check, stop varying single-contact parameters and require either opposition supplied by immobilizing material well away from the separation point, or a mechanically verified free fabric boundary with visible interior passage between plies.
skill_update.rationale: This iteration contributes a genuinely new and reusable negative result that the existing skill does not cover. The existing guidance stops at rejecting a closure whose engaged height collapses onto the surface plane; it does not say what to do when a planner reasons past that gate and deliberately closes below the surface. That reasoning is superficially compelling and will recur, so the library should record that it was tried and produced the identical empty-jaws outcome, closing off the last single-contact parameter rather than leaving it to be rediscovered. The addition stays high-level, names no coordinates or API calls, and does not duplicate hold-checkpoint-timeout-recovery, which governs escalation thresholds and infrastructure acknowledgement rather than closure-depth reasoning.
